title: Black Pepper

seo.title: Black Pepper (Maricha, Kali Mirch) - Benefits, Uses and Safety
seo.description: Learn about black pepper, or maricha, including its botanical identity, Ayurvedic properties, traditional uses for cough and Kapha congestion, dosage and safety.

short_description: Black pepper is a pungent, heating spice traditionally used in small amounts to kindle Agni, reduce Kapha and help clear cough and respiratory congestion.
full_description: Black pepper is the dried fruit of Piper nigrum, known in Ayurveda as Maricha. It is sharp, light and heating, and is a classical Kapha-Vata pacifying spice. In household practice a pinch is often taken with honey for productive cough, or boiled with tulsi and ginger as a tea for Pratishyaya and Kasa.

recommended_dosage.decoction: Use a pinch in 30-50 ml tea
recommended_dosage.extract: Use only as directed by a qualified practitioner

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_effect: Traditionally considered balancing for Kapha and Vata; it readily aggravates Pitta if overused.

key_benefits.benefit: Traditionally used in small amounts to help clear mucus and ease productive cough.
Kindles Agni and may reduce Ama that feeds Kapha in the airways.
Used with honey or in teas with tulsi and ginger for seasonal congestion.

therapeutic_uses.use: Traditionally used for Kaphaja Kasa (wet cough) and Pratishyaya.
Used as a pinch with honey, or in decoctions with ginger and tulsi.
A component of Trikatu, a classical digestive and Kapha-reducing combination.

safety_and_contraindications.safety: Use only small culinary amounts; excess can burn the throat, worsen reflux or aggravate Pitta.
People with ulcers, severe gastritis, or those taking medicines should consult a qualified healthcare professional before using concentrated pepper.
Not suitable as a bulk powder for children; keep pinches small and seek advice for infants.
